name: Mineral Red
lede: Mineral Red is a muted brownish red from Ridgway's 1912 color nomenclature, a descriptive name rather than the record of a single pigment.

sections.title: A descriptive name
sections.body:
Ridgway printed Mineral Red as a plate color in 1912 [1]. The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 later placed it in the grayish red block, and Maerz and Paul list it too [1]. Our books do not explain why Ridgway chose the name, and searching them for the phrase also turns up chance word-pairs, such as "mineral" at the end of one sentence and "red" at the start of the next [2].

In pigment history, though, "mineral red" is an old trade name: the Pigment Compendium lists it as a synonym for red lead (lead tetroxide), and notes that "orange mineral" had largely overlapping meaning and use [3][4]. Red lead was also the base for some heavy eosin lake pigments [5]. We do not claim the Ridgway swatch was drawn from red lead [3].

sections.title: The swatch
sections.body: The swatch is scanned from an aged Ridgway plate, so it is approximate [1]. Its neighbors include [[venetian-red]], [[indian-red]] and [[rosewood]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The color matches 85 paintings in the ColorHub archive, about 0.36%, as photographed [6]. It appears more often than expected in works from around 1910 and 1900 [6].
